summary: Preserved the candidate's generic-template fallback and deferred-tool routing while correcting its demonstrated capability-detection false positive. Native support now requires a Jinja comparison of a content item's type with tool_reference, not merely unrelated AST token presence.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before against the unchanged candidate logic: capability detection returned true and actual conversion plus strict Jinja rendering raised ValueError: Unexpected item type in content.
Passing-after counterexample: both capability classification and actual conversion plus strict rendering passed (2 tests).
Final combined regression run passed 77 tests and 5 subtests, covering generic fallback, deferred discovery gating, native GLM-style behavior, and independent boundary cases.
Lint did not start because the prepared interpreter has no ruff module.
The complete patch contains no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and correction are confined to CPU-side Anthropic request conversion and Jinja AST/rendering behavior; no GPU kernel or model execution is involved.

remaining_limitations: No model weights or full HTTP server were used; transport, model generation, semantic accuracy, and distributed execution were not evaluated.
No native rebuild was performed because no native source changed.
The prepared interpreter lacks ruff, so focused lint could not start; unit regressions and git diff --check passed.
